title: Nanocost Strata panel and pricing policy tiles
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, interactive 'Nanocost Strata' panel in Redwood Console that surfaces token-level spend across multiple axes (role: system/user/assistant, token type: prompt/completion/embedding, model family, route, and customer segment). The panel must support fast in-console export (CSV & NDJSON), inline pricing simulations via 'pricing policy tiles', and tight integration with rollouts so product owners can preview cost impact of model swaps or quantization. This ticket covers prototype artifacts, engineering handoff notes, and a lightweight A/B test plan for display density and export defaults.
design_notes: Primary view uses a horizontal strata metaphor: stacked micro-sparklines per timeslice to show marginal cost contributions across token categories.
Pricing policy tiles are compact cards that let users select a model variant + pricing band and immediately show simulated monthly spend delta for selected filters.
Default aggregation window is 1h with quick toggles for 5m/1h/24h to surface microbursts without killing performance.
Export options include: CSV (tabular rows per invocation), NDJSON (line per event preserving token-breakdown), and XLSX (summary + pivot-ready tabs).
Accessibility: ensure colors for strata pass AA when combined with hatch patterns; tiles expose aria-labels for screen readers.
Mobile: collapse strata into a single stacked sparkline with drill-to-breakdown on tap; pricing tiles become a horizontal carousel.
Performance trade-off: server-side pre-aggregation for 1h and 24h; client pulls 5m microburst data on demand to avoid heavy queries.
Privacy: token-level export must mask any user-supplied content; include a toggle to exclude raw text by default.
decisions: Use stacked line + area micro-sparklines instead of donut breakdowns for trend readability.
Add inline simulation: user can apply a pricing tile to current filters and get immediate 'Projected spend impact' estimate.
Export default will be NDJSON for event-fidelity; CSV/XLSX available as secondary choices.
Expose a role filter (system/user/assistant) as a primary facet to make prompt vs completion attribution explicit.
Keep 'Show raw tokens' off by default and require explicit permission with audit log entry when enabled.
Make pricing tiles composable so multiple tiles can be compared side-by-side for A/B rollout planning.
Integrate with rollout UI: when users preview a rollout that changes model variant, show a channel in the tile labeled 'rollout-preview'.
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Patel): Love the pricing tile simulation — request: show absolute delta and % delta in same view for quick decisioning.
Eng (Marco Ruiz): Concern about backend cost to materialize 5m microburst queries for orgs with high ingestion; suggested on-demand sampling endpoint.
Security (Rina Gupta): Must add audit log entry when enabling raw-token export and ensure KMS policy checks before download.
Design review (Ethan Park): Tighten spacing in tiles; add an affordance for 'compare up to 3 policies' with a keyboard shortcut.
Support (June Lee): Recommend adding CTAs and help tips linking to 'how we calculate token cost' doc to reduce support load.
